name: the-overview-carries-the-space-pane-out-of-frame
description:
The report is that opening the Overview slides its pane in but leaves the space content where it was, so the two overlap instead of trading places.

A rAF sampler in the sidebar records, on every frame of the open and again on every frame of the close, the root's clientWidth, the rail's translateX, the box of the first two rail panes, and the box and shown state of the pinned favourites grid.

The rail was never the defect. It held its two panes exactly one pane width apart on every frame, and the panes traded places as they should. The grid over them was the defect, twice over.

First, markProfileSpan filtered the Overview's empty profile id out of the spanned pair, so a glide onto the Overview read as a same-profile span, the grid's transform was cleared, and it sat at the sidebar edge over the arriving pane for 54 of 189 frames. Second, the grid's offset was computed from at rather than the drawAt the rail was painted with, so on the way back it kept sliding through the settle overshoot while the rail stood still, ending 211px from its own pane.

One frame per direction is still stale, the frame the sidebar width snaps between 220 and 380. On that frame every transform in the sidebar was computed against the old width, the rail's included, so the readings below skip it and slips-are-width-changes records how many there were.

Reopened: the rail and the grid were right, but the two rows hoisted out of the rail were not. The address row and the extensions strip sit over the space pane and only faded, so they stood still while the pane they belong to left.

Sliding them out was the first answer and it was the wrong one. Every transform in the sidebar is sized in the root's clientWidth, and the browser changes that width across the same gesture. The width-snap probe shows it arriving in a single frame, 220 to 380, with the rail's own translate still sized in 220 - so a slide comes apart on exactly that frame, which is the flicker and the pop that manual testing found.

The space content now shrinks and fades away while the Overview grows and fades in. A scale and an opacity need no width, so the width change cannot reach them. The whole crossing is one custom property, --ov-share, written on the element the root and the strip share, and every surface derives its own scale and opacity from it. The *-chrome-tracks-its-space readings pin that derivation on all four routes, and they no longer skip the width-change frame, because there is nothing left on that frame to skip.

The pane readings moved from 380 to 395 with that change and stayed correct. A pane parked off the crossing is scaled to .92 about its own centre, which puts its left edge 15px further in on a 380px sidebar. The rail still holds its panes one pane width apart. The grid readings now weigh what can be seen. It rests 8px inside its own pane, which is the lead padding, holds that while it is fully there, and drifts in as it fades: 1px off at half opacity, 28px by the time it is at a thousandth. The drift itself is unexplained and tracked on its own task. It is bounded here rather than asserted away, at 10px over the frames where the grid is at least half visible, and the whole range stays on the record in grid-geometry-across-the-crossing. The overlap reading is bounded the same way, because a grid at 0.056 opacity covers nothing anyone can see.

The crossing readings take their window from --ov-share rather than from the rendered opacity. Once the rail settles the crossing rules come off and the address row eases back over its own .16s, so a window taken from opacity ran on past the gesture and read that ease as drift.
